result:
I've planned round 230 as the RETRO for rounds 215–229, including the whole-screen review. It changes no app code. Decision: **CONTINUE**.

**Round 229 accepted.** C passed it in a real browser at both viewports (15 rows, `browserVerified` and `realVerified` true), and gate 229 published it as `5da0f50` on both remotes, which is the new baseline. CALM-2a is done.
- C's one Low (C-R229-01: the Loop button's reason is unreachable by keyboard) and gate suggestion 1, which is the same issue, are now one entry under the new task SYS-5.
- Gate suggestions S2, S3 and S5 became deferred Lows that CALM-2b or CALM-3 may fix early; S4 becomes a CALM-3 C check.
- Neither reviewer left an architecture note.

**Gaps I found:**
- **SABA-B-7 was never recorded.** Saba's approved envelope dB-taper fix (Medium) appeared nowhere in `backlog.json` or `feature-status.md`. It is now queued after CALM-3 and before PERF b-ii, as the policy orders. No round was lost, because SABA-B-8 is still in progress. New lessons L41 and L42 cover it.
- **Doc 170 still says "In Progress".** The final stage of its feature passed in round 221, but no task ever updated the earlier stage's doc. Round 231 fixes the line, and L28 now covers this case.
- **Round 229's Escape recipe never worked.** Escape does not clear a time selection here; an empty-lane click does. This is recorded as a harness fact, and L29 now requires B to run every recipe in the browser first.

**Numbers (window 215–229):**

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| C PASS / FAIL | 13 / 2 (215, 216) |
| Gate | published 12, skipped 2, failed 1 (226) |
| Cost | $357.83 |
| Re-do rounds (217, 225, 227) | $50.27 |
| B planning median | $10.58 (threshold ~$12, not exceeded) |

Every number comes from scripts in `b-round-229/`, run on the backlog copy taken before my edits. Retro 215 failed C partly on that ordering.

**Retro 215 experiment:** gate and root raised 0 stale-status findings (baseline 8), so the hypothesis was not refuted, but the evidence is weak. Doc 170 met the experiment's own stop condition, which is why L28 was tightened.

**What C checks in round 230:**
- Recompute every retro number and trace every cause to a quoted line.
- Check the IDs behind SYS-5, the SABA-B-7 queue position and doc 170.
- Check the lessons, that every change is phrased only as a proposal for Saba, and the screen candidates against their screenshots, with one browser probe.
- Run the auth guard and a short Studio smoke test at both viewports.
- Round 231 is CALM-2b if it is planned before 2026-10-30, otherwise REGRESSION.

**Other changes:**
- **`lessons.md`** went from 57 to 51 lines: L23, L26, L28 and L29 amended, L41 and L42 added. Nothing was retired: the tech lead suggested retiring three font lessons, but there were no font rounds in this window to test them.
- **Screen review:** 10 candidates for Saba in `user-review/screen-review-230.md`, from the design-philosopher and first-visit-host reviews. None will be implemented without his answer. One candidate I first read as a bug (a stem sound landing on the Music track) was my capture script clicking the wrong spot; a follow-up probe confirmed the track header works.
- **SYS-5:** a new systemic task to make disabled buttons keyboard-reachable so their reason can be read. It covers the transport toolbar, the metronome and the library Add button, closes four Lows, and is queued after SABA-B-7.
- **Root request:** `b-round-229-checkpoint-request.md` asks for an architecture check on how the envelope curve is stored and scheduled, before SABA-B-7 starts. It doesn't block anything before then.

**Records:**
- `tasks/round-229.md` is an exact copy of the previous task.
- `backlog.json` is at v215, with decisions D-29z292 to D-29z298; `feature-status.md` is updated.
- The store tree hash check still passes and `git status` is empty.
- The advisor was available and I used it before and after the work.
